AR.name: Maqui
AR.citation: Genuinely native to the Andean region of Argentina (EFSA Novel Food dossier summary; Encyclopedia MDPI), not merely an import. Harvested wild by Mapuche communities on both sides of the Chile-Argentina border

CL.name: Maqui
CL.citation: Core native range, from the Coquimbo Region to Aysen (EFSA Novel Food dossier summary). Mapuche-derived alternate names also documented: clon, queldron, koelon, maquei. Considered a sacred plant by the Mapuche people, used for centuries before recent global 'superfood' commercialization

DE.name: Maqui
DE.citation: Direct loanword used in the global superfood/supplement trade (analogous to acai or goji), not an independently-coined German name; the species is not native to Germany

ES.name: Maqui
ES.citation: Direct loanword retained in Spanish-market superfood/supplement trade; the species itself is not native to Spain

FR.name: Maqui
FR.citation: Direct loanword used in the French superfood/supplement trade; the species itself is not native to France

GB.name: Maqui berry
GB.citation: WebMD; direct loanword retained in UK supplement/health-food trade, distinguished from other unrelated 'superfood' berries such as acai, goji and blueberry

US.name: Maqui berry
US.citation: WebMD; regulated as a food by the FDA. Also documented as Chilean wineberry. Commercialized in the US following the global rise of 'superfood' antioxidant berries
